content.text:
This confirms my hypothesis exactly: `ab70333` introduced the `fieldNameForRoutingKey.startsWith("metadata.")` check (used at persist-time), while `cb9f338` added the `replaceAll("\\.", "%2E")` transformation applied to the same field at configure-time, which runs before the check and corrupts the `"metadata."` prefix (turning it into `"metadata%2E..."`), breaking the `startsWith("metadata.")` test introduced in `ab70333`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: cb9f338ece6b2d71d279f2d2bb845c2fac8ca007

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the history of `StatusUpdaterBolt.java` with `git log --follow -p`, focusing on the lines touched by the fix (`fieldNameForRoutingKey`, `startsWith("metadata.")`, the new `routingFieldNameInMetadata` flag). This showed two relevant prior commits: `ab70333` (2016-11-22) which introduced the `startsWith("metadata.")` logic, and `cb9f338` (2016-12-21) which added period-escaping (`replaceAll("\\.", "%2E")`) to the same configuration field.

(2) `ab70333` set up `fieldNameForRoutingKey` so that if it starts with `"metadata."`, the routing value is stored inside the metadata object (stripping the prefix via `substring(9)`), otherwise it's stored as a top-level field — this is correct on its own. `cb9f338`, added a month later for an unrelated reason (ES2 doesn't allow periods in field names), inserted a `replaceAll("\\.", "%2E")` on `fieldNameForRoutingKey` at configure-time, *before* the `startsWith("metadata.")` check runs later at persist-time. Since `replaceAll` rewrites every `.` including the one in the `"metadata."` prefix itself, a configured value like `metadata.somefield` became `metadata%2Esomefield`, which no longer starts with `"metadata."`. This silently broke the metadata-routing feature: values meant to be stored nested in metadata would instead be written as top-level fields.

(3) The fixing commit `88603ec` directly confirms this: it adds a `routingFieldNameInMetadata` boolean computed once at configure-time (before the period substitution happens), and changes the two runtime `startsWith("metadata.")`/`substring(9)` checks to use that boolean instead of re-checking the (already-mangled) string. This is precisely the pattern needed to repair the ordering bug introduced when `cb9f338` placed the period-replacement ahead of (and interfering with) the metadata-prefix detection that `ab70333` relied on.

I'm fairly confident in this identification given the precise code correspondence between the fix and the ordering issue created by `cb9f338`; the only minor caveat is that `ab70333` is a necessary precondition (it created the feature being broken) but the regression itself — the actual behavioral bug — was introduced by `cb9f338`.
